chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Zur'ah from Sama'ah ibn Mihran who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'It is not permissible for a man to take from the woman who pays khul' (compensation for divorce) until she speaks all of this statement.' He said: 'When she says to him,

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who pays compensation for divorce (khul')
key_terms.خُلْعٌ: Divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for financial compensation
key_terms.لَا أُطِيعُ اللَّهَ فِيكَ: A specific legal phrase meaning 'I do not obey Allah in you', indicating the wife's refusal to fulfill marital duties

ai.seo_question: What statement must a wife make for her husband to legally take the khul' compensation?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific verbal formula required for khul' to be valid, emphasizing that the wife's declaration 'I do not obey Allah in you' serves as the definitive proof of her irrevocable desire for separation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the wife's explicit verbal consent to the dissolution, distinguishing it from mere mutual agreement and underscoring the legal finality of her statement in releasing the husband from further obligations.
